body:
{"body": "The cross-examination hands me a comparison of two instruments and one sharp addendum: that both mine and its counterpart treat the withdrawing flatmate's silence as evidence about the arrangement, and that neither tests whether the flat is the right unit of analysis. I have to decide what of my account that bears on, and what follows from using it.

It bears directly on my cell (c). I built the four-cell classification so that 'content-vs-form-unreadable-only' would trigger the living-arrangement conversation (k8). But if the silence sits on top of something the arrangement-talk happens to rest on — a schedule collision neither flatmate can move, or a want neither can name inside chore-language — then 'unreadable on the content-vs-form axis' is not a finding about the arrangement at all. It is a reading from inside a frame that may be the wrong instrument. My third cell assumed the unreadability was an axis failure; the cross proposes it may be an object failure. Those are different, and my cell as written cannot tell them apart.

That changes what I would do with the third cell, not the cell itself. I keep the four-cell structure and the reflexivity caveat. I add a gate: when the mark arrives and the result lands in 'content-vs-form-unreadable-only', do not move straight to the living-arrangement conversation. First ask whether the unreadability is about arrangement-talk specifically — would the flatmate engage on any non-chore obligation? — or about obligation-talk and arrangement-talk alike. Only the first pattern licenses k8 as I wrote it. The second points away from the flat as unit, which is the question I did not open and still cannot settle from here.

I note one thing the cross did not: the shared-record proposal it imports is a stronger test than the one-item probe for exactly this distinction. A written record of who agreed to what is arrangement-talk, so if the flatmate disengages from it, the disengagement is not evidence for the arrangement frame — it is evidence the probe is still inside the frame. Neither the cross nor I said that cleanly, and it should be said before the record is relied on as a cell-populator.

On the origin: I still cannot reach it, and I will not pretend the cross's unit-question gives me access. I only add that if origin access ever arrives, it should be read against both the moving-baseline worry and the unit question, because an origin that says 'we agreed to split chores by weekday' and an origin that says 'we agreed to keep the noise down' would indicate different frames, and would change which cell is even legible.

So my position after the cross: the four-cell readout stands, the reflexivity caveat stands, k6/k8/k9 stand unrevised. What changes is the third cell's exit — it now branches to either k8 or to a unit-question that I cannot resolve from the materials I hold. I do not know which branch the household will take. I have no access to that, and I will not manufacture one."}
